Every AAA RPG (actually any genre,really) either quickly or before long ends up being, despite proclamations of how "non-linear" it would deem itself, an ugly mess of fraud.

This one is particularly ugly -- more than half the time if I discover or take care of a situation without being led to it by the linear narrative, I am "rewarded" with a series of "mission accomplished" ding-dings and unexplained material rewards...

Okay, so since that is all at least not detrimental, I have been able to just sigh and move on.

But now I decided to take on the secondary mission of "The Devil In the Well" (close enough)...

I knew what was up; I knew what I would like to try and do to fix it; And I was able to solve the "mystery" way out of order, and without having to follow the silly series of hand-holding, nose-ring-pulling hints... then I was forced to "find" (press "Witcher Sense" button) the goddamed clues, each in the ordained order laid out by the non-linear system...

And, now, worst of all, it seems, according to the "self-narrative" of Geralt, I cannot solve the problem without getting stupid and violent.

I don't want to Spoiler a fucking thing.

I want to Spoiler. End of problem.

...

I do realize that anticipating every possible move a player may make, especially in what order, is impossible. But this game is really quite terrible in trying to do so.

N'est–ce pas?

So... I play on... and murder the murdered wretch... then find out I'm slightly sorry after all according to the quest-wrap-up...

And then not much later I am forced, despite purposefully putting my sword away, to murder a bunch of drunks to "save" and end-up actually horrifying my favorite pub-mistress...

Then I'm forced to let the smug toadies at the emperors shave my beard. This after I'm given the dialogue "choice" of refusing...

Very poor pretense, Witcher 3.

Which game are you comparing it to?
